title: Maximum guidance depth (Inference, Limit, Operator, Task, Textable, Numeric)
documentation:
## Settings domain
The functional subsystem a setting governs. Domains group settings into UI sections
and into the runtime modules that consume them.

Model inference parameters: temperature, top-k, top-p, max tokens, sampling and
guidance policies.

## Settings concern
The kind of decision a setting captures. Concern groups settings by the shape of the
value they hold, regardless of which subsystem (domain) consumes them. Useful for
generic UIs that render concern-by-concern.

A numeric ceiling, floor, or capacity bound: max concurrent operations, minimum
free memory, maximum tokens. The value is typically numeric.

## Settings audience
Who is expected to read or modify the setting. Audience determines which UI surface
exposes the setting (end-user preferences vs operator console vs developer tuning).

Operator-level configuration. Visible in deployment-tuning surfaces. Adjusting these
settings affects throughput, resource usage, or model behaviour and should be done
by someone familiar with the workload.

## Settings scope
The lifecycle attachment of a setting value. App-scoped settings persist across
launches; task-scoped settings apply for the duration of a single cap or workflow
execution; model-scoped settings attach to a specific model artifact.

Applies for the duration of a single task or workflow run. May default from app
preferences but can be overridden per execution.

## Textable
Coercion marker indicating the value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text.
Strings are textable trivially; integers and booleans are textable via their
string form; structured values are textable when JSON-serialised. Binary blobs
(images, audio, raw bytes) are NOT textable — converting them to text requires
explicit transformation that may be lossy.

The value is faithfully representable as UTF-8 text without loss.

## Numeric
Coercion marker indicating the value supports numeric operations (addition,
comparison, ordering). Independent of `textable`; a numeric value is often
also textable (an integer is encodable as text), but neither implies the
other in general.

The value supports numeric operations.
